assumptions_and_boundaries.name: IterMut::new
assumptions_and_boundaries.rationale: The Rust 1.96 target body is exactly the delegation `IterMut::new(self)`. The harness verifies that delegation against a narrow source-backed constructor contract while leaving the constructor's `NonNull::from_mut`, pointer addition, ZST `without_provenance_mut`, and unsafe raw-pointer representation to a separate boundary.

assumptions_and_boundaries.name: core::ptr::NonNull<T> and raw `end_or_len` iterator representation
assumptions_and_boundaries.rationale: Rust stores `IterMut` as a start pointer and an end pointer or ZST length. The target `iter_mut` body only delegates to `IterMut::new`, so the harness uses an opaque lifetime-marker representation and confines pointer/provenance obligations to the constructor boundary.

assumptions_and_boundaries.name: slice_iterator_view::<IterMut<'a, T>, T>
assumptions_and_boundaries.rationale: The private constructor boundary relates the returned iterator to the generated shared iterator-view vocabulary; the target postcondition is not assumed directly.
